hero.subtitle: A structured information platform you run yourself — schema, access control, workflows and an admin UI in **one binary**, with your entries stored as **files you own**.

items.title: Model it
items.body: A **space** organizes your data into folders. A **schema** describes a valid entry, and dmart checks every write against it.

items.title: Store anything
items.body: JSON entries, files and tickets all go in. Each one lands as a plain file on disk and as an indexed row in PostgreSQL or SQLite.

items.title: Control who sees what
items.body: Roles and permissions are checked on every request, down to the folder, the action and the field.

items.title: Find it fast
items.body: One query language searches everything you stored: filter on any field, sort, and page through the results.

items.title: Use it everywhere
items.body: A REST API, SDKs for Python, TypeScript, Dart and C#, an admin UI, a catalog, and an MCP server for AI agents, all from one binary.

items.title: Unified Data
items.body: Entries, attachments, metadata — all in one model. Structured and unstructured data, seamlessly.

items.title: Powerful Search
items.body: Full-text search, filtering, aggregation. Powered by SQL full-text blazing performance.

items.title: Access Control
items.body: Role-based access, granular permissions down to folder and entry level. Secure by default.

items.title: Extensible
items.body: Plugin architecture, webhooks, custom workflows. Adapt DMART to any use case.

sections.title: Runs Where a Backend Normally Can’t
sections.body:
One self-contained binary, compiled ahead of time. No runtime to install, no container required, no separate frontend to deploy — the admin UI ships inside it.

Measured on a **Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W** with 416 MB of usable RAM, serving with PostgreSQL alongside it on the same board: **106 MB** resident for the whole stack, ~14 ms warm reads, and four concurrent logins served with a bounded peak that is fully reclaimed. A 10-hour continuous write soak held memory flat — a plateau, not a slope — with no OOM and no thermal throttling. The same binary runs on a server.

items.title: 106 MB
items.body: dmart + PostgreSQL, idle, of 416 MB

items.title: ~14 ms
items.body: warm read, 5,000-entry fixture

items.title: 0.6 GB/day
items.body: written under sustained load — ~460 yr on a 100 TBW card

items.title: Files are the source of truth
items.body: Entries live as plain files on disk. The SQL store is a **rebuildable index** over them — copy the folder, rebuild the index anywhere, and you have your system back.

items.title: Standard formats, not a vendor schema
items.body: Payloads are JSON, constrained by **JSON Schema Draft 7** and evaluated by a standard library. There is no dmart-specific type system to migrate out of.

items.title: Self-hosted, AGPL-3.0
items.body: Run it on your hardware, in your network, air-gapped if you need to. No per-seat pricing and no hosted service you depend on.

items.title: Define Your Space
items.body: Create spaces and organize data into hierarchical folders — just like a file system.

items.title: Store Anything
items.body: Create entries with JSON payloads, attach files, add metadata. Schema-validated or free-form.

items.title: Query & Discover
items.body: Full-text search, filter by any field, sort, paginate. All through a consistent REST API.

items.title: Integrate Everywhere
items.body: Use official SDKs for Python, TypeScript, Dart, and C#/.NET. Or call the REST API directly.

items.title: Features
items.body: Unified data management, collaboration tools, and advanced search capabilities.

items.title: Why DMART?
items.body: Transform data from a liability into an asset. Own your data, no vendor lock-in.

items.title: Technical
items.body: ASP.NET Core on .NET, PostgreSQL-backed. A single Native-AOT binary — built for simplicity and speed.

items.title: Drivers
items.body: Official client libraries for Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Dart/Flutter, and C#/.NET.
